KEY MESSAGE 1...Overall pattern remains the same, though with
guidance finally converging on a solution with regards to
coastal storm track and timing. Deep upper trough is digging 
into the southern plains and taking on an increasingly neutral 
tilt, while a separate low and attendant jet streak dives out of
the Canadian prairies and tracks towards the Ohio River Valley.
The latter two features are forecast to undergo a complex 
interaction over the eastern CONUS through Thanksgiving, with 
the Plains trough digging further into the Gulf Coast and taking
on a negative tilt as it interacts with the OH Valley low. We 
will see a similar evolution at the mid- levels with two potent 
shortwave troughs.

This overall pattern favors surface cyclogenesis along the 
Southeastern coast starting this morning, where a stalled
boundary is noted on regional radar reflectivity off the SC
coast. Trends continue to favor an inland tracking low tonight
into early Thanksgiving Day as the upper low becomes negatively
tilted, bringing the low north and then NNW into ctrl NC. The 
low will be deepening as well, with strong vorticity advection 
arriving late today and maximizing overnight, with strongest 
winds and heaviest rain. Wind speeds have thus increased, and 
with 850MB winds reaching or exceeding 70 kt tonight, some of 
the heavier showers may mix down some stronger gusts even 
inland, which is why wind adv has been expanded. Nearer the 
coast, with the vicinity of the Gulf Stream just offshore, the 
strong E winds should advect this more efficient mixing toward 
the OBX and Downeast, where wind gusts may reach or exceed 60 
mph, esp in the heavier convective showers, and thus the High
Wind Warning is in effect tonight. With PW's surging to aoa 2" 
combined with the intense lift, widespread mod to heavy rain 
rates arrive, with 25/00Z LPMM REFS guidance now up to 
widespread 4-6" with locally higher amts through Thanksgiving
morning. Best chance of seeing 6+" appear to be the srn coast 
where strongest FGEN occurs this evening. 

Risk of thunder overall remains low with only marginal
instability available - less than 500 J/kg for the mainland. 
Still, areas closer to the coast, esp the OBX and Downeast, 
will have to be monitored for a localized svr threat, as strong 
cells over the Gulf Stream could approach the islands providing 
an iso tornado or waterspout threat overnight tonight. 

Heavy rain and wind diminish rather abruptly Thursday morning as
the low pres arrives and shunts strong lift and gradient out
ahead of it to the north and east of ENC, and flood watch and
wind headlines will follow suite and end prior to noon. Winds
turn S then SW rather light, but then increase Thu night through
Fri as strong pres falls occur with upper low pivoting through
the region.

KEY MESSAGE 2...ENC is currently experiencing the next round of
king tides this week with an increase in antecedant water 
levels. These are expected to peak the next several days and 
then begin tapering off Friday and esp the weekend, and will be 
slightly higher than the cycle that occurred in October. Water 
levels will remain elevated through today with the gradient in
place.

Tonight cont to be much more concerning as the approaching low 
pres brings and even further inc in strong winds veering to the
east with storm force winds adjacent to the OBX and strong gales
up the inland rivers (Pamlico and Neuse), and brings the threat
for significant coastal flooding for these areas. Most tidal 
locations across ENC are likely to see at least minor to 
moderate impacts, with a window overnight for major impacts up
these main stem rivers. With the decrease in winds on Thursday 
expected, the flood threat for the inland rivers and southern 
Pamlico Sound may begin to ease, but oceanside impacts will cont
on the OBX into late week. Then, as swrly winds inc Thu night
through Fri, the threat for OBX soundside flooding increases
with minor to locally moderate impacts possible.
